flags: AI provisions are a minor part of a broader preauthorization-process reform (posting requirements, decision deadlines, authorization validity periods, formulary continuity, payment rules).
aiSoleBasis coded from § (6)(e)(iii), which bars sole reliance on 'recommendations from any other source' — broader than AI-specific; AI is not named in that subsection.

humanReview coded required-final (the determination itself must be made by an individual exercising independent medical judgment); appeals must ALSO be reviewed by a licensed physician (or pharmacist for drugs) per § (6)(c)-(d) — multi-value, lossy under single-enum rule.
Decision deadlines — 'no later than seven calendar days' (§ (5)(a)) and 'no later than 72 hours' for urgent care services (§ (5)(b)) — have no matching param in the insurance-adm vocabulary.

Authorization validity minimums — 'may not be less than 12 months' for chronic/long-term care (§ (7)(b)) and 'may not be less than six months' for outpatient services (§ (7)(e)) — have no matching param in the vocabulary.
No penalty or enforcement provision in the text; department receives reports and 'may make rules to implement Subsection (9)(b)' only — exposure omitted (silence is silence).
Reporting subsection 31A-22-650(9)(b) and rulemaking subsection (13) are repealed July 1, 2029 (§ 63I-1-231(2)-(3)); bill takes effect January 1, 2027 (§ Section 3).
